Zig.reasoning: Six of six, but only after the substitution that global_rules / official_project_table._resolution_procedure_if_a_field_is_wrong_or_missing requires. The frozen official_implementation_repository for Zig, github.com/ziglang/zig, is not the project's repository at the evidence cutoff: ziglang.org links only codeberg.org/ziglang/zig as Source, the GitHub copy's last push is 2025-11-27 and its newest issue is 2026-04-11, so scoring N6 on the frozen URL would have recorded 'no issue in the 90-day window' and given Zig 80. The substitution rule was applied exactly as written (replace with the resource the language's own official homepage links to as its source repository, record the substitution and reason) and was checked against the other nine languages: none of the other nine official repositories was found to be wrong, so no other substitution was made.

cross_language_consistency_note: One indicator set, one evidence source per indicator, and one procedure were applied to all ten languages in the frozen collection order with Quidra last. For every language the same six questions were asked in the same way: N1-N3 were answered only from documents published inside that language's frozen official_docs_root (never from a third-party site such as cppreference, MDN or a book); N4 was answered only by executing the installed toolchain's help on this host, for all ten including Quidra; N5 required a channel designated inside the official docs root plus one message with a machine-readable date inside 2026-06-19..2026-09-17; N6 required one tracker item created inside the same window whose author is absent from the project's own published maintainer roster. Where a rubric phrase admitted more than one reading, the reading was fixed in writing (R1-R4 above) before Quidra was examined and applied unchanged to every language. Checking the ten assignments together: the nine languages at 100 each satisfy all six indicators on the same kinds of artifact; C++ at 80 differs from them by exactly one observable fact (no first-party install-to-run tutorial for C++), not by a difference of standard; Quidra at 60 differs from C++ by two further observable facts (no designated community channel anywhere in its documentation root, and zero issues from anyone other than its single maintainer) while matching all four documentation indicators. No two languages with the same observable evidence received different levels: Java and Kotlin, whose implementation repositories both have GitHub issues disabled, were both scored on the project-designated external tracker with the roster test, and both satisfied N6; Zig, whose frozen repository turned out to be a stale mirror, was handled by the frozen substitution procedure rather than by an unverified pass. No incumbency discount was applied: the mature languages' complete first-party documentation sets and demonstrably active forums and trackers were scored at full value, and Quidra received no allowance for being an experimental 0.2.0 core.
limitations: Accession occurred on 2026-09-19, two days after the frozen evidence cutoff of 2026-09-17. Documents (N1-N4) are dated at or before the cutoff by their own version strings; for N5 and N6 only items created on or before 2026-09-17 were used, although later items were visible in the same listings. Nothing in this record depends on post-cutoff activity.

C++ N3 is the single most contestable call in this metric. Four first-party candidates were examined and rejected for the stated reasons; an auditor who accepts llvm.org/docs/GettingStarted.html (whose worked example is a C program compiled with clang and run) or isocpp.org/get-started (which points to third-party tutorials) as satisfying N3 records C++ at 6/6 = 100. Microsoft's and the GNU Project's C++ tutorials would satisfy N3 outright but Microsoft and the GNU Project are not in C++'s frozen official_project_set, which lists only WG21, the LLVM Project/Clang and Apple.

Swift N2 'at a stated version': Apple's Swift standard library reference states per-symbol platform availability rather than a Swift release number (the companion first-party book states '(6.4 beta)'). An auditor requiring an explicit Swift version on the API reference itself records Swift at 5/6 = 80.

Quidra N2 granularity: the entries are module-level prose sections in docs/spec/language.md that name the exported items and give signatures for many of them, not generated per-symbol pages like the other nine languages'. R4 admits module granularity because the indicator's own parenthetical lists modules as items; an auditor who requires generated per-symbol entries records Quidra at 3/6 = 40.

Zig N6 required the frozen substitution procedure. Scored on the frozen URL github.com/ziglang/zig - a mirror whose last push is 2025-11-27 and whose newest issue is 2026-04-11 - Zig would be 5/6 = 80. The substitution to codeberg.org/ziglang/zig follows official_project_table._resolution_procedure_if_a_field_is_wrong_or_missing and the same check was run for the other nine repositories, none of which needed substitution.

TypeScript N2 depends entirely on the frozen official_project_table placing the Node.js project inside TypeScript's official project set; Microsoft publishes no per-symbol reference for the lib.*.d.ts standard type declarations. Without that frozen membership TypeScript would be 5/6 = 80.

Channels that are not publicly readable without joining (Discord servers for TypeScript, Zig and C++/LLVM; the Kotlin Slack; IRC) could not supply an N5 message for any language and were not used for any language. Kotlin's and TypeScript's N5 therefore rest on Stack Overflow tags designated by their official sites, while the other eight rest on a project-run forum or mailing list; both routes are admitted by the indicator text.

Java N6's primary reporter account, 'webbuggrp' (Webbug Group), is the JBS account through which reports submitted via the public bug-report form are filed, so the individual reporter's identity is not exposed; it is nonetheless an account absent from the Project jdk roster. A named-individual corroboration in the same window is recorded (JDK-8392520, Leonid Kuskov / lkuskov, 2026-09-16).

N5 and N6 counts for the GitHub-hosted projects were taken from the GitHub search API's total_count for the window (Python 1397, LLVM 3191, Rust 1136, Go 1316, TypeScript 318, Swift 350, Quidra 0); those totals are contextual and no level depends on them, only on the single cited in-window item.
